questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Chemical analyses of both Harappan copper artifacts and Omani copper ingots revealed traces of which element, confirming maritime contact?
questions.explanation: Both Harappan copper artifacts and copper from Oman contain characteristic traces of nickel, suggesting a common geographical origin.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Why was Alexander Cunningham unable to recognize the great antiquity of the Harappan seal presented to him in the nineteenth century?
options: A) He mistakenly attempted to place it within the chronological timeframe of the 6th-4th centuries BCE Ganga valley civilizations
B) He believed the seal was a modern British toy
C) The inscription was completely worn away
D) He assumed the seal had been imported from medieval Venice
questions.explanation: Cunningham, using Chinese Buddhist pilgrims' itineraries, thought Indian civilization began in the 6th century BCE Ganga valley, missing Harappa's 3rd millennium BCE antiquity.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: The earliest inscriptional reference to the self-immolation of a widow (Sati), dated to 510 CE during the reign of Bhanugupta, was found at:
questions.explanation: The Eran pillar inscription of 510 CE in Madhya Pradesh records that Goparaja died in battle and his wife burned herself on his funeral pyre.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In the Adi Parva of the Mahabharata, the marriage between the Pandava prince Bhima and the forest-dwelling demoness Hidimba represented an alliance:
options: A) Outside the orthodox Brahmanical varna and gotra norms
B) Following the strict rules of Brahma marriage
C) Approved by the elders of Hastinapur in court
D) Involving a massive royal dowry
questions.explanation: Hidimba belonged to the non-Aryan Rakshasa clan; the marriage defied orthodox endogamous varna prescriptions, producing Ghatotkacha.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Where did Vardhamana Mahavira pass away (attain Nirvana) at the age of seventy-two?
questions.explanation: Mahavira passed away at Pavapuri (Pawapuri in Nalanda district, Bihar) around 468 BCE.

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Al-Biruni translated the classical Sanskrit mathematical and astronomical treatise 'Brahmasphutasiddhanta', originally composed by:
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni studied and translated the works of Brahmagupta into Arabic, praising his advanced planetary models.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Which of the following female Bhakti poets of Tamil Nadu was celebrated as an Alvar saint whose hymns expressed deep bridal mysticism towards Lord Ranganatha?
questions.explanation: Andal regarded herself as the bride of Lord Vishnu (Ranganatha), composing the famous Tiruppavai.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The military defeat of Vijayanagara at the Battle of Talikota in 1565 occurred during the reign of which Aravidu de-facto ruler?
questions.explanation: Rama Raya, the ambitious chief minister and de-facto ruler, led Vijayanagara's forces at Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota) where he was captured and executed.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: What was the term for the large tract of land in the Rajmahal Hills demarcated by the British government in 1832 for the permanent settlement of the Santhals?
questions.explanation: Damin-i-Koh (literally 'skirts of the hills') was demarcated with masonry pillars in 1832 for the Santhals to practice settled agriculture.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India who invited Mahatma Gandhi for extensive talks in early 1931, leading to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Lord Irwin held bilateral talks with Gandhiji, resulting in the famous Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed in March 1931.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: A clay seal discovered at Lothal bears an engraved image depicting which maritime object, highlighting Harappan overseas navigation?
options: A) A sailing ship with a central mast and oars
questions.explanation: Seals and terracotta amulets found at Mohenjodaro and Lothal clearly depict masted sailing vessels used for riverine and sea voyages.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In Ashokan epigraphy, which Major Rock Edict strictly prohibited animal slaughter for public sacrifices and festivals, as well as curtailing it inside royal kitchens?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict I prohibited animal sacrifice (yajna) and festive gatherings (samaja) where meat was consumed.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: Which of the following post-Mauryan rulers was a staunch follower and royal patron of Jainism who recorded his victories in the Hathigumpha inscription in Odisha?
questions.explanation: King Kharavela of the Chedi dynasty recorded his military victories and liberal endowments to Jain monks in the Hathigumpha rock inscription.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The famous Pali Buddhist text 'Milindapanho' (Questions of King Milinda) consists of philosophical dialogues between the Indo-Greek King Menander and the Buddhist sage:
questions.explanation: Milindapanho records the penetrating dialogue on Buddhist metaphysics between King Menander (Milinda) and the monk Nagasena.

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: In his seventeenth-century account, why did Francois Bernier refer to the Mughal Empire as a 'state of beggars and barbarians'?
options: A) He found that no hospitals existed in Delhi and Agra
B) He argued that crown ownership of all land eliminated private property, creating a degraded countryside and destroying municipal commerce
C) He witnessed frequent peasant mutinies across Punjab
D) He noticed that Europeans were barred from riding horses
questions.explanation: Bernier characterized the Mughal king as a 'king of beggars and barbarians' because the absence of private property supposedly reduced the populace to poverty.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The twelfth Alvar Vaishnava saint Tondaradippodi composed verses praising devotion to Lord Ranganatha, in which he famously asserted that:
options: A) Only those who know the four Vedas can attain liberation
B) Devotees from outcaste communities who serve Vishnu are superior to learned Brahmanas lacking devotion
C) All images in temples should be replaced with sacred fire
D) Women should not be permitted into temple sanctuaries
questions.explanation: Tondaradippodi declared in his verses that an outcaste devotee who loved Vishnu was worthy of deep reverence, unlike an arrogant Brahmana.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The iconic Stone Chariot (Ratha) at Hampi, standing inside the courtyard of the Vitthala temple, is actually a shrine dedicated to which divine mount?
questions.explanation: The stone chariot inside the Vitthala temple is an exquisite monolithic shrine dedicated to Garuda, the vahana of Lord Vishnu.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Under the Mughal revenue system, the system of 'Ghalla-bakhshi' (or Batai) referred to:
options: A) A cash assessment based on past five years' prices
B) The physical division of the harvested crop between the state and the peasant in agreed proportions
C) A tax levied on village artisans and shopkeepers
D) An auction of provincial tax revenue to highest bidders
questions.explanation: Ghalla-bakhshi or Batai was crop sharing, where the grain was physically divided after harvest in the presence of state officers.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: In the Deccan countryside, why did British revenue officers fix high tax demands under the Ryotwari settlement in the 1820s and 1830s?
options: A) They sought to force ryots to abandon farming and join the British navy
B) They based revenue on theoretical land fertility surveys assuming ideal yields, ignoring droughts and price drops
C) They had to pay reparations to Maratha Peshwas
D) They wanted ryots to cultivate tea and coffee exclusively
questions.explanation: British surveyors calculated revenue demands based on estimated maximum soil fertility, resulting in crippling assessments that ryots could not pay during lean monsoons.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: During the 1857 uprising in Bihar, the aged zamindar Kunwar Singh joined the rebellion after British authorities:
options: A) Imprisoned his eldest son for cow slaughter
B) Deprived his family of estate rights and threatened to auction his lands due to debt and tax arrears
C) Ordered the demolition of his ancestral temple
D) Drafted his retainers into service in Afghanistan
questions.explanation: Kunwar Singh was deeply aggrieved by British revenue exactions and government interference in his Jagdishpur zamindari management.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: In the 1937 provincial elections held under the Government of India Act 1935, which party formed a coalition ministry with the Congress in the North-West Frontier Province?
options: B) Khudai Khidmatgars (led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan)
questions.explanation: Dr. Khan Sahib and the Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts) swept the NWFP elections and formed the provincial government.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, who eloquently advocated the inclusion of a strong central unitary authority, stating that 'an unstable and weak center would invite external invasion and internal partition'?
options: B) K.M. Munshi and Gopalaswami Ayyangar
questions.explanation: K.M. Munshi, Gopalaswami Ayyangar, and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer forcefully argued that historical lessons required an invincible Central government.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Which of the following ports on the Coromandel coast served as a major early historic port trading actively with the Roman Empire, as confirmed by excavations of amphorae and Arretine pottery?
questions.explanation: Excavations at Arikamedu revealed Roman amphorae (wine containers), Arretine ware, and Roman intaglio seals, proving intensive maritime commerce.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Which Bhakti tradition in Maharashtra, centered on the temple at Pandharpur, emphasized collective congregational singing (kirtan) and pilgrimage (vari)?
questions.explanation: The Varkari tradition, guided by saints like Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, and Tukaram, emphasized the annual pilgrimage (vari) to Pandharpur.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the seventeenth century, how did the village community in northern India penalize members who committed serious breaches of caste endogamy or occupational rules?
options: A) Confiscation of private property by the Mughal governor
B) Expulsion from the caste community (excommunication) and loss of communal ties
C) Sentence to life imprisonment in provincial forts
D) Forcible conscription into the imperial artillery
questions.explanation: Caste panchayats exercised formidable authority; their ultimate sanction was excommunication, which severed all social, matrimonial, and dining links.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton described the landscape of the Rajmahal Hills in 1810-1811 as being in a state of transition because:
options: A) The Ganges had permanently shifted its course ten miles east
B) The East India Company had opened tea plantations across Bhagalpur
C) Santhals were progressively clearing dense forests with iron axes and ploughs, driving the Paharias deeper into the rocky summits
D) Indigo factories had caused total soil exhaustion
questions.explanation: Buchanan documented that Santhals were felling Sal forests and turning valleys into settled rice fields, pushing the retreating Paharias higher into the hills.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: During the Quit India Movement in August 1942, who operated an underground clandestine radio transmitter in Bombay to broadcast news of protests to the nation?
questions.explanation: Usha Mehta and her brave young colleagues ran the 'Secret Congress Radio' from changing locations in Bombay until arrested in November 1942.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which committee was headed by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, playing the decisive role in drafting the fundamental rights and tribal area protections?
options: C) Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel chaired the 54-member Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal Areas.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In early historic India, what did the term 'Varna-samkara' signify in Dharmashastric legal literature?
options: A) The renunciation of Vedic sacrifices by forest hermits
B) The spiritual purification ceremony for kings
C) The intermixture of varnas caused by inter-varna marriages, leading to the creation of new jatis
D) The coronation ceremony of an imperial monarch
questions.explanation: Varna-samkara refers to the intermixture of varnas resulting from anuloma (hypogamy) and pratiloma (hypergamy) unions.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: What was the significance of the title 'Hindu Suratrana' (Hindu Sultan) adopted by the Rayas of Vijayanagara in their royal inscriptions?
options: A) It showed that the empire was a direct province of the Delhi Sultanate
B) It proved that the rulers had formally converted to Islam
C) It indicated that Vijayanagara rulers adopted and adapted prestigious contemporary Islamic titles of sovereignty to assert their paramount political authority
D) It was a derogatory label given by Portuguese merchants
questions.explanation: Hindu Suratrana was a Sanskritization of 'Sultan'; it reflected the cultural and political borrowing from contemporary Deccan Sultanates to assert imperial paramountcy.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Which of the following British visual depictions of 1857 was published in the satirical magazine 'Punch', representing British justice as a vengeful goddess trampling rebel sepoys?
questions.explanation: Tenniel's famous cartoon 'Justice' in Punch depicted a colossal goddess of justice wielding a sword and shield, crushing mutineers beneath her feet.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, which forest community in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh staged a 'Forest Satyagraha', sending their cattle into reserved forests without paying grazing fees?
options: C) Chenchus and local tribal cultivators
questions.explanation: In Guntur and the Palnad hills of Andhra, tribal peasants defied colonial forest grazing laws by organizing massive forest satyagrahas.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the craft production technologies discovered at the Harappan settlement of Chanhudaro:
1. Steatite micro-beads were formed by molding a paste of ground steatite powder mixed with an adhesive.
2. Carnelian's brilliant red color was achieved by baking yellowish raw nodules at various stages of manufacture.
3. Drill bits used for perforating carnelian beads were made exclusively of soft marine shell.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because bead drills were made of hard specialized stone (chert/jasper) and copper, not soft shell.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayaga Prashasti), which of the following frontier kingdoms (Pratyanta rajas) is explicitly mentioned as paying tribute, obeying imperial commands, and performing obeisance before Samudragupta?
options: C) Samatata, Davaka, Kamarupa, Nepala, and Kartripura
questions.explanation: Line 22 of the Prayaga Prashasti lists Samatata (Bengal), Davaka (Assam), Kamarupa (Assam), Nepala, and Kartripura as frontier rulers who paid homage and tribute.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In ancient Indian legal history, what was the crucial difference between the inheritance rights of women under the Mitakshara and Dayabhaga legal traditions that evolved from ancient codes?
options: A) Dayabhaga banned all gifts of stridhana to daughters
B) Mitakshara abolished the varna system while Dayabhaga enforced it
C) Under Mitakshara, sons acquired coparcenary rights by birth; under Dayabhaga, sons had no coparcenary rights during the father's lifetime, allowing widows to inherit in the absence of male heirs
D) Mitakshara gave 100% of the estate to the youngest daughter
questions.explanation: In Mitakshara (prevalent in most of India), sons inherit by birth; in Dayabhaga (Bengal and Assam), sons inherit only after the father's death, enabling widows to hold property.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Which of the following doctrines encapsulates the fundamental Buddhist concept of the human person as articulated in early Pali suttas?
options: A) The body is an illusion created by demonic forces (Mara) to entrap celestial gods
B) The person possesses an immutable, eternal cosmic soul that is identical with Brahman
C) The individual is an impermanent combination of five aggregates (khandhas): form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, lacking any eternal atman
D) The soul is a physical atom located in the center of the pineal gland
questions.explanation: Anatta (non-self) is a core Buddhist teaching: the self is not an immutable soul but a constantly changing process of five skandhas (aggregates).

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: How did Al-Biruni reconcile his respect for Indian mathematics and astronomy with his criticism of later Brahmanical astronomical texts in the Kitab-ul-Hind?
options: A) He claimed that Indian astronomers could not calculate solar eclipses
B) He asserted that all Indian calculations were plagiarized from ancient Babylonian clay tablets

C) He praised earlier thinkers like Aryabhata and Varahamihira for scientific rigor, but condemned later scholars who diluted astronomical truths with mythological superstitions under theological pressure
D) He argued that Indian algebra was solely derived from Persian court manuals
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni observed that scholars like Brahmagupta knew the scientific cause of eclipses, yet compromised with popular myths (Rahu swallowing the sun) to appease priests.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: In the institutional evolution of Sufism in India, what was the distinction between the 'ba-shari'a' and 'be-shari'a' silsilas?
options: A) Ba-shari'a operated in Bengal; be-shari'a existed exclusively in the Deccan
B) Ba-shari'a was practiced by women only; be-shari'a was restricted to kings
C) Ba-shari'a banned qawwali singing; be-shari'a made musical recitals mandatory five times a day

D) Ba-shari'a orders conformed strictly to Islamic canonical law; be-shari'a mendicants (such as Qalandars and Madaris) deliberately flouted canonical rituals and lived in radical antinomian asceticism
questions.explanation: Ba-shari'a orders (Chishti, Suhrawardi) adhered to the Quranic Shari'a; be-shari'a groups (Qalandars, Haidaris) defied established norms, shaved their hair, and lived in poverty.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question:
Examine the following statements regarding the Mahanavami Dibba in Vijayanagara:
1. It was an enormous square granite platform covered with sculpted relief friezes of war horses, dancers, and royal hunting.
2. Recent excavations revealed that there were no permanent stone chambers atop the platform, indicating it was surmounted by temporary wooden pavilions and canopies.
3. The platform was built exclusively by Harihara I in 1336 to mark the founding of the empire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the platform was constructed in phases, reaching its grand dimensions during Krishnadeva Raya's reign after his Orissa victories.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: What primary ecological and fiscal constraint limited the adoption of the Zabti system across large tracts of eastern Bengal, Sindh, and the Deccan hills during Akbar's reign?
options: A) Akbar forbade land surveying in non-Hindi speaking subas
B) The local cultivators refused to speak Persian with revenue clerks
C) European merchant companies had purchased sovereign rights over delta land
D) Zabti required annual land measurement and stable price data, which was administratively unfeasible in riverine deltas, shifting terrain, and rugged hill tracks
questions.explanation: Zabti depended on accurate annual cadastral measurement; in swampy Bengal, shifting sandbanks, and rocky terrains, Batai or Nasaq (estimation) was used instead.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: In his surveys of eastern India, what was Francis Buchanan-Hamilton's primary mandate from the British East India Company?
options: A) To negotiate border treaties with the Kingdom of Nepal
B) To compile Sanskrit grammars for Christian missionaries
C) To organize military recruitment camps for the Bengal Army
D) To meticulously survey natural resources, minerals, commercial flora, craft technologies, and land revenue yields to identify avenues for commercial exploitation
questions.explanation: Buchanan was dispatched by the Company to assess the economic potential of districts: mapping soils, minerals, crops, forests, and artisans for imperial profit.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Which of the following visual representations of the 1857 uprising portrayed the English general Sir Colin Campbell in a heroic posture, framed by triumphant Highlanders shaking hands with the defenders of Lucknow?
options: A) 'The Storming of the Delhi Gate'
B) 'In Memoriam' by Joseph Noel Paton
D) 'The Relief of Lucknow' by Thomas Jones Barker
questions.explanation: Barker's famous oil painting 'The Relief of Lucknow' celebrated Colin Campbell, Henry Havelock, and James Outram meeting as triumphant saviors of the garrison.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi undertake a historic fast-unto-death in Yerwada Central Jail in September 1932 against the British Communal Award?
options: A) He sought the withdrawal of the Rowlatt Acts
B) He demanded an immediate increase in daily prison rations for satyagrahis
C) He protested against the partition of Bengal
D) He opposed Ramsay MacDonald's provision of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, arguing it would permanently divide Hindu society and institutionalize untouchability
questions.explanation: Gandhiji fasted against separate electorates for untouchables, leading to the Poona Pact with Dr. Ambedkar, which substituted joint electorates with increased reserved seats.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which distinguished member made a celebrated intervention declaring that 'Real freedom can exist only when there is economic justice and equality for the toiling masses', warning against substituting brown oligarchs for white rulers?
questions.explanation: Somnath Lahiri, the CPI member, constantly reminded the Assembly that true independence required radical socioeconomic restructuring to benefit peasants and workers.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding ancient Indian land grants (dana-patras):
1. Inscriptions recording land grants were typically engraved on copper plates (tamra-patra) and handed to the recipient as legal deeds of title.
2. Most surviving land grants from the Gupta period onward were made to Brahmanas or religious institutions like temples and monasteries.
3. The Danguna copper plate inscription records that Prabhavati Gupta granted land along with royal exemptions from the entry of soldiers and royal revenue collectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are historically accurate: copper plates functioned as legal title deeds, most went to religious beneficiaries, and Prabhavati Gupta granted lands with immunities.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In the Manusmriti, what was the severe penalty prescribed for an outcast Chandala who dared to listen to the recitation of the Vedic mantras?
options: A) He was required to shave his head completely
B) He was to be appointed as a temple guard
C) He had to perform a Soma sacrifice
D) Molten tin or lead was to be poured into his ears
questions.explanation: Orthodox Dharmasutras laid down horrific symbolic penalties for untouchables who violated sacred boundaries, including pouring molten lead into their ears.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: In Jain metaphysics, what is the concept of 'Anekantavada' (the doctrine of manifold aspects of reality)?
options: A) Violence is permissible if conducted during defensive warfare
B) God created the universe out of nothingness in six days
C) All souls merge into an impersonal Brahman upon death
D) Ultimate reality is complex and multifaceted, and any single human perspective can capture only a partial truth (Syadvada)
questions.explanation: Anekantavada holds that truth and reality are complex and have multiple aspects; dogmatic insistence on a single perspective leads to delusion.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Which prominent Chishti Sufi saint was famously given the title 'Ganj-i Shakar' (Treasury of Sugar) and settled at Ajodhan (in modern Pakistan), with his verses included in the Sikh Adi Granth?
questions.explanation: Baba Farid (Shaikh Fariduddin Ganj-i Shakar) lived at Ajodhan; his Punjabi verses were revered for their spiritual sweetness and incorporated into the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the urban core of Vijayanagara, what evidence discovered by archaeologists indicates the presence of a distinct Muslim residential quarter?
options: A) An open-air arena for bullfighting
B) A massive Persian cathedral built of white marble
C) Arabic gold dinars minted by Ottoman sultans
D) Tombs, mosques, and residential structures featuring plaster domes and cusped arches located near the northeastern sector
questions.explanation: Archaeological mapping revealed a Muslim residential quarter in Vijayanagara containing tombs, cemeteries, and mosques built with characteristic arches and plaster domes.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which woman delegate presented the National Flag made of silk on behalf of the women of India on 14 August 1947, just hours before independence?
questions.explanation: Hansa Mehta, representing the All India Women's Conference, formally presented the first National Flag of independent India to the Assembly on the midnight of 14-15 August 1947.
